dataIdInfo.idAbs:
The “IRS_Locations” shapefileshows the locations(latitude and longitude) of Indian Residential Schools and student hostels operated by the federal government in Canada. All the residential schools and hostels that are listed in the Indian Residential School Settlement Agreement are included in this shapefile(dataset), as well as several Industrial schools and residential schools that were not part of the IRRSA. This version of the shapefile(dataset) doesn’t include the five schools under the Newfoundland and Labrador Residential Schools Settlement Agreement.

The original school location data was created by the Truth and Reconciliation Commission, and was provided to the researcher (Rosa Orlandini) by the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation in April 2017. The "IRS_Locations" shapefilewas created by Rosa Orlandini, and builds upon and enhances the previous work of the Truth and Reconcilation Commission, Morgan Hite (creator of the Atlas of Indian Residential Schools in Canada that was produced for the Tk'emlups First Nation and Justice for Day Scholar's Initiative, and Stephanie Pyne (project lead for the Residential Schools Interactive Map). Each individual school location in the "IRS_Locations" feature layer is attributed either to RSIM, Morgan Hite, NCTR or Rosa Orlandini.

Many schools/hostels had several locations throughout the history of the institution. If the school/hostel moved from its’ original location to another property, then the school is considered to have two unique locations in this dataset,the original location and the new location. For example, Lejac Indian Residential School had two locations while it was operating, Stuart Lake and Fraser Lake. If a new school building was constructed on the same property as the original school building, it isn't considered to be a new location, as is the case of Girouard Indian Residential School.When the precise location is known, the coordinates of the main building are provided, and when the precise location of the building isn’t known, an approximate location is provided.

For each residential school institution location, the following information is provided: official names, alternative name, dates of operation, religious affiliation, latitude and longitude coordinates, community location, Indigenous community name, contributor (of the location coordinates), school/institution photo (when available), location point precision, type of school (hostel or residential school) and list of references used to determine the location of the main buildings or sites.

The dataset is available via York University’s Dataverse. To have access to the IRS Locations reference dataset, please contact Rosa Orlandini at rorlan@yorku.ca, for access, as the references dataset is not yet available for publications.
dataIdInfo.idCredit: The school/hostel location data was collected by the Truth and Reconciliation Commission / National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation, Morgan Hite (Atlas of Indian Residential Schoolsof Canada), Stephanie Pyne (Residential Schools Land Memory Mapping Project) and Rosa Orlandini (Map and GIS Librarian, York University Libraries). The location data and associated attribute data was enhanced, revised and updated by Rosa Orlandini, in consultation with the Archivists at the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation.

attr.attrdef: Unique ID of the residential school or hostel. A unique id was applied to each school/hostel listed Common Experience Payment of the Indian Residential School Settlement Agreement. Residential schools and hostels not included as part of the IRSSA agreement are also included, although the list isn't exhaustive. This version of the data doesn't include provincially run residential schools, nor does it include schools in Newfoundland and Labrador.

Unique ID of the school/hostel location. If the school/hostel moved to another property it is considered to be a unique location. If a new school/hostel building was constructed on the same property, it isn't considered to be a new location. This code contains the school number followed by the location number. For example, Lejac (41) had two locations, Stuart Lake (411) and Fraser Lake (412).

Unique ID of an related (associated) school location. Some schools when they moved formally changed the name and/or ownership. For example, Lac La Biche school closed in 1898, and the staff/students were moved to the first location of Blue Quills School, which was near Saddle Lake.

Primary authority name of the residential school or hostel used by the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation. The name was adapted and based on the Independent Assessment Process and Common Experience Payment Lists.

attr.attrdef: The name of school location. Many residential schools had more than one location throughout their history. In that case, the name of the school name is provided with the location name in brackets. For example, Portage La Prairie (First Location) and Portage La Prairie (Second Location). When there is the same name for multiple schools a dash (-) symbol is used to distinguish the schools from each other. For example, St. Michael's - Alert Bay and St. Michael's - Duck Lake.

attr.attalias: Alternative Name of School or Hostel
attr.attrdef: Known alternate names of the school at that location. This was derived from historical documents, IAP and CEP lists, and NCTR data.

The year that the school or hostel location started operations. The dates were derived from documents provided by the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation, Church archives and Library Archives Canada.

The year that the school location or hostel location closed. The dates were derived from documents provided by the National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation, Church archives and Library Archives Canada.
The latitude coordinate of school/hostel location. The latitude coordinate is provided in decimal degrees. This field can be used with the longitude to map the location.
The longitude coordinate of school/hostel location. The longitude coordinate is provided in decimal degrees. This field can be used with the latitude coordinate to map the location.

The individual or group cited for determining the location of the school or hostel. The coordinates are placed, whenever possible on the site of the main school/hostel building at the location. Hite, refers to Morgan Hite (Residential School Atlas), NCTR (National Centre for Truth and Reconciliation), Orlandini (Rosa Orlandini), RSIM (Residential School Interactive Map).

Description of the geographical coordinates of the school location. It describes where the main school building or hostel is situated, as well as other key features on the site. For some sites the location of previous buildings on the site are indicated.

The type of school location. "School Location" indicates that it is the location of the Residential School. "Hostel Location" indicates the location of the student hostel associated with a day school. "Hostel and School Location" indicates that the day school and the hostel were on the same property/site. "Mission and School Location" indicates that the mission and the school are on the same site, and the exact location of the school is unknown. "Community Location" indicates the geographical coordinates are for the community, and the precise location of the school/hostel is unknown. This field was created by NCTR and updated by Rosa Orlandini.

The precision of the geographical coordinates for the school/hostel location. "Precise" indicates that the main school/hostel building is within 25 metres of the point. "Approximate" indicates that the precise location of the main school building/hostel building is not known and documentation exists that describes the approximate location the school. "Predicted" indicates that location of the school/hostel building is unknown and no documentation has been found to support where the school was located. This field was created by Morgan Hite and updated by Rosa Orlandini.

The precision in kilometres for the school/hostel locations. 0 indicates precisely located schools; The value indicates that the school is likely located within the specified distance of this point. For example, 0.5 indicates that the school building is likely located within 0.5 kilometres of the point. This field was created by Morgan Hite and updated by Rosa Orlandini.
The URL of the photo of the school or hostel, if available. This field can be used to display a thumbnail image of a school.
The title of the photo of the residential school or hostel. The photos are primarily of the school/hostel buildings or aerial views of the school/hostel sites.
The attributed source of the photo.

The status of the main school building or hostel at that location. (1) "Present" = Building is still standing as of 2019. (2) "Not Present" = Building is not present on the site. (3) "Remains Present" = The foundations or the ruins of the main school building are present. (4) "Unconfirmed" there are multiple buildings still present on the site and/or community and the precise main building cannot be determined. This field was created by Morgan Hite and updated by Rosa Orlandini.
Name of the municipality that the school was located. In rural and remote areas, the nearest municipality is listed. This field was created by NCTR and updated by Rosa Orlandini.

dataLineage.statement:
In April 2017, the National Centre for Truth and Reconcilation provided the researcher (Rosa Orlandini) with a uneditted spreadsheet of Indian Residential Schools in Canada. The data for this project was edited and modified in Excel. The coordinate information for the schools were cleaned by Rosa Orlandini in May 2017. From June 2017 until July 2017, the methodology to verify the NCTR locations dataset, as well as locations from other sources (Morgan Hite and Stephanie Pyne). The schools in Ontario were used as a pilot and from August 2017/September 2017, the primary source and secondary source that showed the location of the residential schools were found, consulted, and documented, and the location and attribute information for each Ontario school was updated and enhanced.
Further refining of methodolgy occurred in October 2017, resulting in two datasets (1) school locations database and (2) school locations reference database (the locations reference dataset is a separate dataset/spreadsheet, but can be joined using the Reference IDs in this database.
From October 2017 to July 2018, the locational information, primary/secondary sources, attriibute data for the remaining provinces and territories were completed. From August 2018 to February 2019, all of 181 entries (locations records) were verified and edited. The Master dataset was created in February 2019.
In March 2019/April 2019, an excel spreadsheet was extracted from the master database. A final agreement between Rosa Orlandini and the National Centre for Truth and Reconcilation was established in March 2019, to distribute the data as part o the creative commons licenses. To pepare the data for integration into a Geographic Information Systems, the field names were modified and described. The dataset was exported as a CSV file and imported as a feature layer in a Geodatabase. The metadata was described for the feature layer IRS_Locations.
The feature layer and completed metadata data was exported into an shapefile called "IRS_Locations.shp". The location description information in the attribute/field "location description" were truncated for some records due to the field size limitation of 255 characters. The full location description of the location for each record can be found in the file IRS_LocDescription.csv. The IRS_LocDescription.csv can be linked to this IRS_Locations.shp dataset using the Unique ID of the location. The IRS_LocDescription.csv is packaged with the file, IRS_Locations.shp.
